title: Add Splunk HEC connector with optional ACK support + structured error classification
author: Diego Santos
description: Summary: Implements the Splunk HEC sink connector for audit-export, including optional HEC ACK mode for stronger delivery confirmation. Adds batching limits (max events, max bytes, flush interval) and structured error classification so the worker can apply consistent retry/backoff + DLQ behavior. Context: We need a production-ready first sink for the SIEM-ready audit export beta (Splunk is the most common initial request). Connector must be explicit about delivery semantics: at-least-once overall, with additional confirmation when Splunk HEC ACK is enabled. What’s included: (1) SplunkHECClient with send() that supports HEC event endpoint and optional ACK polling, (2) batching policy with size and time bounds to protect memory/latency, (3) error taxonomy (auth/throttle/bad_request/server/network/unknown) + mapping to retryable vs non-retryable, (4) metrics hooks (counters + histograms) and safe logging (no token leakage), (5) tests (unit + mock-server integration) covering 2xx/4xx/5xx/429, partial failures, ACK timeout, and request-channel header handling. Notes on semantics: Without ACK, success is HTTP 200/201 from /services/collector/event. With ACK enabled, we treat the initial POST as accepted and then poll /services/collector/ack until all ackIds are confirmed or we hit timeout (retryable). This does not provide exactly-once, but reduces false positives during transient Splunk issues. Config: Adds connector config fields splunk.hec.endpoint, splunk.hec.token (secret), splunk.hec.index (optional), splunk.hec.source (optional), splunk.hec.sourcetype (optional), splunk.hec.ack_enabled (default false), splunk.hec.ack_timeout_ms, splunk.hec.batch_max_events, splunk.hec.batch_max_bytes, splunk.hec.flush_interval_ms. Follow-ups (out of scope): wire full connector metrics into the global exporter dashboard pack; add circuit-breaker behavior at worker level (tracked in ENG-13932); document recommended Splunk dashboards/queries (owned by CS docs).

conversation: Kevin Osei (review): ACK flow looks good. Two asks: (1) please ensure we never log the HEC token, even at debug, (2) classify 400 vs 401/403 distinctly so control plane can surface actionable errors in Console.

Diego Santos (author): Added token redaction in the HTTP request logging helper + updated errors.go to map 400 -> bad_request(non-retryable) and 401/403 -> auth(non-retryable). Also added tests for both cases.

Marcus Lin (review): On ACK polling: can we bound the polling loop and add jitter to avoid thundering herd if many destinations enable ACK at once? Also confirm TLS verify is not disabled anywhere by default.

Diego Santos (author): Added maxPollAttempts derived from ack_timeout_ms and a fixed polling interval with +/- 20% jitter. TLS verify remains default; no InsecureSkipVerify usage. Added a unit test to ensure client uses default transport settings.

Sean Gallagher (review): Batching limits: can we cap both events and bytes and enforce a hard ceiling to prevent a single giant event from blowing up the batcher? Also would like metric names aligned with exporter conventions (connector_requests_total, connector_failures_total, connector_latency_ms).

Diego Santos (author): Implemented dual caps: max_events + max_bytes; if a single event exceeds max_bytes we fail fast with bad_request and include an error code for DLQ annotation. Renamed metrics to match conventions and added labels: destination_id, status, error_kind.

Ethan Park (review): Minor: add a note in docs that ACK requires Splunk HEC to have enableACK=true and that it can increase end-to-end latency. Also mention how we set X-Splunk-Request-Channel and why.
Diego Santos (author): Updated docs/connectors/splunk-hec.md with prerequisites + latency tradeoff and a short explanation of request-channel header usage for correlating ackIds.

Diego Santos (author): Increased test server response determinism and reduced polling interval in tests only; re-ran CI.
release_notes: New: Splunk HEC destination connector with configurable batching (max events/bytes + flush interval).
New: Optional HEC ACK mode for stronger delivery confirmation via ack polling.
Improved: Structured error classification (auth/throttle/bad_request/server/network) to drive retries/DLQ behavior.
